key_terms.sense: overcharging or undercharging in a sale
key_terms.definition: The prohibition against selling an item for more, or buying it for less, than its market value. A discrepancy of a sixth gives the wronged party a claim, which he may raise within the time needed to show the item to a merchant or relative.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Rav Chisda rules that when prices shift after an ona'ah sale, only the exploited party may cancel it, and not the party who exploited him, even though he now loses.

key_terms.definition: Terumah and tithes must be separated from produce of the same kind (min) as the produce they exempt. Separating from a different kind for another is ineffective.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The Rabbis count wine and vinegar as one type for terumah, following R. Ela that inferior produce may be separated for superior. For buying and selling, everyone agrees they are two types.

key_terms.definition: A mode of acquiring movable property in which the buyer pulls or draws the item toward himself. It is effective only in a place such as an alleyway or a courtyard shared by both parties, not in the public domain.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The Mishnah rules that pulling acquires produce and measuring does not. To fit Abaye and Rava's rule, the Gemara reads the Mishnah's "pulled" as pulled from the public domain into an alleyway.

key_terms.definition: A mode of acquiring movable property in which the buyer lifts the item. It is effective in every place, even in the seller's domain.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Flax, which is usually carried, is acquired only when the buyer carries it from place to place. Abaye and Rava state that lifting acquires everywhere.

key_terms.sense: alleyway as a domain for acquisition
key_terms.definition: A side area off the public thoroughfare that is neither fully public nor anyone's private property. People may leave their belongings there, and pulling acquires there.
key_terms.on_this_daf: R. Asi and R. Ya'akov give conflicting reports of R. Yochanan's ruling on produce measured into an alleyway. The reports are reconciled as the buyer's basket, which acquires, versus the ground, which does not.

key_terms.definition: A person's vessel acquires for him items placed into it, much as his courtyard does, when it rests in a place where it can serve him.
key_terms.on_this_daf: R. Zeira limits R. Yochanan's alleyway ruling to produce measured into the buyer's basket. The Gemara upholds this reading and applies it to the partners' courtyard as well.

key_terms.definition: A person's property acquires for him items that are placed in it, as though his own hand had taken them.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The perspicacious buyer rents the spot where the produce lies, so that the place becomes his and acquires the produce for him before the seller can retract.
